subject: Real-time SLA pathway evaluation for PulseHealth pilot
messages:
From: Samir Shah <samir@pulsehealth.ai>
To: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Katherine Li <katherine@pulsehealth.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Nov 2028 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Intro call - latency/throughput notes

Thanks for the quick sync this morning, Ethan. A few clarifications from our side so you can recommend the right deployment path:

- Primary flow: 95% of requests are single-turn inference for real-time triage (avg payload ~1.2KB).
- QPS: steady 60 QPS during business hours, expected peaks to 220 QPS for ~10 minutes (1-2x/day).
- P50 latency goal: <= 60ms, P95: <= 180ms. Tail is critical for user experience.
- Throughput + batching: we can tolerate batching up to 40ms additional server-side latency for significant cost savings.

We are sensitive to data controls; PH handles PHI-like telemetry (pseudonymized), so a VPC option is good to have but not mandatory for the pilot. Security questionnaire attached (we'll need answers before pilot).

Can you send a recommended pilot approach (Hosted with fallback to Dedicated, or Dedicated-only) and a simple SOW + estimated cost range? Also: we'll populate the latency_profile_template.xlsx you mentioned and return it by Monday.

—Samir
VP Product, PulseHealth

Samir — thanks, that helps a lot. Confirming next steps from our side: 

1) I'll draft two pilot paths for review:
   - Path A (Hosted-first): Hosted API pilot with a staged canary to Dedicated if we observe P95 > 200ms or sustained QPS > 120 for >30m.
   - Path B (Dedicated baseline): Start on Dedicated GPU pool with reserved capacity sized for 220 QPS peaks.

2) I'll attach a short SOW and the latency_profile_template.xlsx (please fill and return).
3) Marissa and Ben will weigh in on cost/commitment tradeoffs and propose a pricing envelope.

A couple of quick questions to finalize sizing: can you confirm average token count per request (rough tokenization estimate rather than raw bytes) and whether you need streaming responses?

Attaching: pilot_sow_draft.pdf (stub), latency_profile_template.xlsx (stub)

Looking for a short call next Wed to agree the pilot path. I copied Marissa for decision escalation and Ben for commercial.

—Ethan
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Team — quick internal note before we produce the recommendations:

- For Path A (Hosted-first) include explicit SLA gates when we flip to Dedicated: P95 sustained > 200ms for 15m, or sustained QPS > 140 for 30m. Define rollback and warm-up windows.
- For Path B (Dedicated baseline) include capacity autoscale policy and a burst pool (30% extra) for daily peaks.
- We should run our internal microbenchmark using 80-token and 250-token profiles (Ethan: can you run on the same model family we plan to propose and capture P50/P95/P99?).

Ben — please draft a two-option commercial that maps to the above, keeping the pilot a 30-day commitment with an option to convert to a 3- or 12-month reserved commitment. I'll attach a short bench_plan.md for Ethan's run.

Marissa
Director, Solutions (on behalf of Sales Eng Leadership)

Subject: Pilot commercial options & next steps

Hi Samir — following Marissa's guidance, two commercial options for the 30-day pilot:

Option 1 — Hosted-first Pilot (recommended for fastest time-to-value):
- 30-day hosted pilot, shared capacity; canary window to Dedicated based on SLA gates.
- Pilot fee: $9,500 (covers engineering support + burst credits).
- Conversion: 3-month dedicated commitment starts at $45k/month with a 10% discount for annual commit.

Option 2 — Dedicated Baseline Pilot:
- 30-day Dedicated reserved pool sized for peak (220 QPS) with 30% burst capacity.
- Pilot fee: $28,000 (covers reserved capacity & support).
- Conversion: reserved pricing and standard onboarding credit applied.

Next steps: sign pilot SOW and security addendum. I've created the DocuSign envelope (link below) for a non-binding SOW acceptance so we can schedule provisioning.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/abcdefg

Happy to jump on a call Wednesday Nov 22 to walk through the tradeoffs and finalize which path.

—Ben
